articles.headline: Chargers' Mike McDaniel takes blame for team's offensive struggles
articles.description: Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel blamed himself Thursday for the team's offensive struggles.
articles.body:
EL SEGUNDO, Calif. -- Los Angeles Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel blamed himself Thursday for the team's offensive struggles.

"I'm fully responsible," he said. "... I spend zero time trying to avoid blame. It's quite the opposite."

McDaniel, fired in January after four years as the head coach of the Miami Dolphins, was brought in this offseason to make the Chargers offense among the league's best. The team's offense had been an Achilles heel the last two seasons, scoring only one touchdown over two playoff losses, and McDaniel was viewed as one of the final pieces for this team to reach true championship contention.

His addition gave the Chargers the fifth-best odds to win the Super Bowl ahead of this year in ESPN's Football Power Index.

Instead, the Chargers offense has been a disaster. Quarterback Justin Herbert is second in the NFL in interceptions, and his QBR (27.4) is the second worst in the NFL, only higher than Giants quarterback Jameis Winston. They rank 29th in points per game (14.7) and tied for fifth in turnovers (6).

Sunday's loss to the Buffalo Bills was the latest nightmare for this team. The Chargers defense forced five turnovers, while the Chargers only committed one and somehow lost the game. McDaniel said it was the first time in his career he could remember losing with a plus-four turnover differential.

"We were the reason we lost the football game," McDaniel said. "And you gotta pull your weight in this league."

Still, McDaniel said he isn't discouraged. He pointed to the volatility of the NFL and his own example: Three years ago, his offense scored 70 points in a Week 3 win over the Denver Broncos.

"People want to tell you that you're the greatest offensive history of the National Football League," McDaniel said.

And the media did, including one piece published in September 2023 by CBS Sports that wondered if it was an overreaction or reality that "Miami has the greatest offense in the Super Bowl era." But McDaniel's offense flopped in the postseason, as Miami lost in the first round to the Kansas City Chiefs 26-7.

"I'm not minimizing it; it's not acceptable to me," he said of the offense. "But also not creating a fake gland that ignores annual history," he said. "There's a team that you guys can think of right now, either way, that everyone was crowning."

McDaniel also defended Herbert, who received a rare public critique from coach Jim Harbaugh earlier this week. "Nothing has changed with Justin Herbert," McDaniel said, adding that he feels like he better understands Herbert after three weeks.

"I think at this point I have a much better understanding of things that lead to him making good plays," he said. And yet McDaniel said Herbert's play has to improve, just like everyone else's on the team, and said so does his coaching.

articles.headline: Saints putting RB Travis Etienne (hamstring) on IR
articles.description: The Saints are placing running back Travis Etienne on injured reserve, which will sideline him for at least the next four games.
articles.body:
The New Orleans Saints are placing running back Travis Etienne Jr. on injured reserve, which will sideline him for at least the next four games.

Etienne, who has a hamstring injury, suffered his injury in the Saints' Week 3 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders.

Etienne had been on the injury report leading up to the game with a hamstring issue but participated fully in Friday's practice. Coach Kellen Moore, who announced that Etienne would miss time with his injury, said the injury occurred on the same leg as the one that had been bothering him during the week.

Etienne had a season-high 19 carries for 57 yards before the injury. After he left, carries were split between Alvin Kamara (six carries after Etienne's injury) and Kendre Miller (four carries after Etienne's injury).

Kamara, who missed time with a knee injury in September, had nine carries in his season debut against the Baltimore Ravens in Week 2 over Etienne's eight carries, although the Saints almost exclusively used Etienne as the main rusher in the first half of the Raiders game.

Kamara, Miller and rookie CJ Donaldson will likely all be used in the Saints' Week 4 game against the Atlanta Falcons on Monday night. Kamara is second on the team with 18 carries for 51 yards despite missing the season opener, while Miller, who was a healthy inactive against the Ravens, is third with 13 carries for 44 yards and a touchdown.

The 2026-27 NBA season officially kicked off Sept. 22 as the Houston Rockets held their media day, before the Dallas Mavericks followed suit Friday.

The other 28 teams in the association joined them Monday, ahead of training camps beginning for most teams.

How will LeBron James and Jaylen Brown look in their new Philadelphia 76ers uniforms? What will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first media day away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their first impressions?

Check back here for all the latest buzz, news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders, with the latest info at the top:

Quick links:

Free agency grades | Trade grades

Trade tracker | Transactions | Offseason buzz

Depth charts | Trade machine | More

Oct. 1

Mitch Johnson excited about Billy Donovan's role with Spurs

San Antonio Spurs coach Mitch Johnson likes what he's seen so far at training camp from new lead assistant coach Billy Donovan.

"I don't want to be naive enough to think I'm going to tell you what a 61-year old Hall of Fame coach like Billy Donovan and his resume can bring to the table," Johnson said. "I'm excited he's here. He's a tremendous person, great personality, fits in seamlessly. He's got worlds of experience and he's an extremely hard worker. He's not kicking up his feet and telling stories. He's rolling his sleeves up and getting his hands dirty. He's going to help all of us and probably me, specifically, a ton this year."

Donovan joined the staff in July, replacing former lead assistant Sean Sweeney, who left San Antonio to take the head coaching job in Orlando. Sweeney ran the Spurs' defense last season, helping it improve from 25th to third in the NBA in defensive rating (110.4).

Donovan won't be tasked with taking on Sweeney's responsibilities, according to sources, however. San Antonio brought in Donovan to lean on his experience on both ends of the floor, as well as his vast knowledge of the NBA and college games.

A member of the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame class of 2025, Donovan joined the Spurs after 11 seasons as an NBA coach with the Chicago Bulls and Oklahoma City Thunder, after capturing two college basketball national titles in 2006 and 2007 with the Florida Gators. -- Michael C. Wright

Shead agrees to three-year extension in Toronto

Guard Jamal Shead has agreed to a three-year, $24 million extension with the Toronto Raptors, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Shead averaged 6.6 points and 5.6 assists per game last season.

Nuggets add Nembhard on two-way deal

Guard Ryan Nembhard has agreed to a two-way contract with the Denver Nuggets, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. We know many of you compete in superflex formats that invite/covet second quarterbacks in starting lineups, and these rankings account for that. It might look odd to see the lowest-ranked fantasy passers ahead of typical RB2 and WR2 options, but the potential scoring impact demands it.

If your league is a standard flex, note that rankings without QBs appear below the superflex rankings. However you prefer to play, good luck this week!

These ranks have been refreshed to take out players from Thursday's Steelers-Browns game.

-->

Week 4 superflex rankings (includes quarterbacks)

 1. Jahmyr Gibbs, RB1 @ CAR

Six touchdowns in three games is quite the feat. It's LaDainian Tomlinson stuff (2006).

The league leader in fantasy points seems unstoppable, regardless of matchup.

articles.headline: Manchester City guilty charges explained: Premier League's options, how appeal works, more
articles.description: Tuesday's news that the Premier League found Man City guilty of 100-plus charges of breaking financial rules is a landmark moment. But what comes next: what punishments are on the table, and how does the appeals process work?
articles.body:
Manchester City's guilty verdict on 114 charges of breaking Premier League financial rules is a landmark moment in global sport.

City continues to assert their innocence and have signaled their intention to appeal before Friday's deadline. But the Independent Commission's verdict could hardly have been more damning, accusing the club of "sham" contracts involving its Abu Dhabi owners as part of a "disguised funding scheme" that contributed to inflating revenues and reducing costs by over £900 million. Witnesses in City's defense were accused of dishonesty, and the club was found to have "clearly intended to circumvent" Premier League rules.

The breaches relate specifically to a nine-year period (2009-18), but the shockwaves permeate far beyond. Pep Guardiola's trophy-laden legacy is in doubt. The Premier League's reputation and viability is in the balance. Rivals may seek retribution through compensation claims, triggering challenges that could last for years.

Meanwhile, City's punishment is yet to be determined. Under Section W, Rule 54 of the Premier League's Handbook, they are facing a punishment ranging from a reprimand to expulsion. There could be a fine, a points deduction and a transfer ban.

City's aggressive protestations of innocence only contribute to the widespread uncertainty and reduces the likelihood of all parties coming together to reach agreement on a settlement for the time being. Beyond that, the legal complexities are vast.

ESPN has spoken with one of the United Kingdom's leading law firms, Howard Kennedy, in pursuit of clarity. Partners Kyle Phillips and Lois Langton head the firm's sports group, with Phillips specializing in business crime and regulatory process. On Thursday, the pair talked with ESPN's James Olley to answer some basic questions and follow-ups about what this all means and what's next.

Editor's note: This interview has been edited for clarity and length.

How would you characterize the commission's findings?

Kyle Phillips: I think it's worse than many people expected. The words that were used by the commission in the findings report, caveated with the fact it's very difficult to read because a lot of it is redacted and there's no evidence or appendices that they keep referring to, but the language that they use is very strong.

"Sham" is one point. You've got the disguised payments, sorry -- the "disguised funding scheme," overstating commercial revenue, the amounts involved ... it is all quite shocking. And it is quite a strong statement to say that you find the witness evidence that was given to be "dishonest" -- a powerful word in any decision.

In any regulatory proceedings, it takes a lot for them to use that word.

articles.headline: Spurs' Victor Wembanyama not interested in promoting betting sites
articles.description: Spurs star Victor Wembanyama said Thursday that he isn't interested in promoting sports betting sites.
articles.body:
SAN ANTONIO -- Count Spurs star Victor Wembanyama as one of the professional athletes who isn't interested in promoting sports betting sites.

The Frenchman expressed his view on the subject Thursday after a training camp workout.

"Absolutely not," Wembanyama said when asked if he'd ever consider promoting a sports betting website. "I will never do that. Honestly, I think it's very sad to see some players promote it. Everybody does whatever they want, but without me."

Wembanyama was subsequently asked how he makes decisions about which brands to promote.

"In the past, there was a dimension of money," he said. "Not anymore. Even if I said that, I've refused plenty, much, much more money than I've made for things that were not [in line with] my values. And now, I want to promote things that have a good impact, have a good influence with who I can share messages and values. Obviously, we earn millions and millions. This is not our biggest strength. Our biggest strength is inspiring. I want to inspire in a good way. That's the strongest thing I can do."

Several of Wembanyama's NBA peers currently promote sportsbooks and prediction platforms, including LeBron James, who moved from DraftKings to Polymarket in September, Kevin Durant (FanDuel), who is also an investor in Kalshi and Giannis Antetokounmpo, who became a shareholder at Kalshi back in February.

"The internet is full of opinions," Antetokounmpo wrote in a since-deleted post on X, announcing the move. "I decided it was time to make some of my own. Today, I'm joining Kalshi as a shareholder."

Three-time MVP Nikola Jokic, in 2023, became the first brand ambassador of Superbet in Serbia.

The NBA's collective bargaining agreement treats sports betting operators and prediction markets the same when it comes down to player partnerships. Players aren't allowed to promote betting on any market related to the NBA. But they are allowed to endorse and hold de minimis equity investments in sports betting companies with some restrictions.

Wembanyama, meanwhile, enters his fourth season in the league coming off San Antonio's first appearance in the NBA Finals since 2014. The two-time All-Star last season became the first player to unanimously win NBA Defensive Player of the Year after leading the league in blocks for the third-consecutive season.

Wembanyama, 22, finished third last season in voting for NBA MVP.
